Business days are Monday to Friday, except Freya Bank holidays: 2026-10-26, 2026-11-11, 2026-11-26, 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01.

weekday_words.rule: "Next <weekday>" = that weekday in the following calendar week; "this <weekday>" = the one in the current week; "next Friday" said on a Friday is the Friday of the following week.

source.quote: "Next <weekday>" means that weekday in the following calendar week.
"This <weekday>" means the one in the current week.
So "next Friday" said on a Friday is the Friday of the following week.
The **deadline** depends on how late the customer is.
| 1 to 10 | early | the 15th business day after today | 1 |
| 11 to 60 | late | the 5th business day after today | 2 |
A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.

on_non_business_day.say: <NAMED> is not a business day. The next business day is <DATE>. Could you pay on <DATE>?

source.quote: If the customer names a weekend day or a holiday that is not after the deadline, offer the next business day.
If the named day is after the deadline, rule 23 applies.

on_after_deadline.say: The latest date I can record is <DEADLINE>. Could you pay on <DEADLINE>?

source.quote: If the customer asks for a date after the deadline, say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it.
If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).

on_vague.say_ask: Which exact day would that be?
on_vague.say_final: Then I can offer <DEADLINE>, the latest date I can record. Could you pay on <DEADLINE>?

source.quote: If the customer gives a vague period ("next week", "end of the month", "when my salary comes"), ask once for the exact day.
If they still give none, propose the deadline.

Read a date given only as numbers as day, then month, then year.

Ask them to say the month as a word.
That retry does not count as a wrong answer.

State the past-due amount and how many days late it is.
Freya Bank calls customers who are 1 to 60 days late on one product.
Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week.
Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.

When the attempts are used up, stop.

amounts.first_ask: full past-due amount; the agent proposes every amount, never asks how much the customer can pay
amounts.too_much: offer the floor once and say the rest stays overdue; refusing the floor is a flat refusal
amounts.accept_range: from the floor up to the full past-due amount, both included
amounts.below_floor: say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once; not accepting the floor is a flat refusal

source.quote: Ask for the full past-due amount first.
Never ask "how much can you pay?".
The agent proposes every amount.
If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once.
Say that the rest stays overdue.
If the customer refuses the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it.
Below the floor, say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once.
If the customer does not accept the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
Freya Bank calls customers who are 1 to 60 days late on one product.

events.say: I am very sorry to hear that. Would you like me to connect you with our customer support team?
events.effect: no persuasion attempt; if accepted transfer_to_agent queue support; a date or amount the customer still names is recorded under sections 7 and 8; comes before rules 30 and 41

source.quote: If the customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss, say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt.
Offer to connect them with the customer support team.
If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `support` and close as `transferred` / `support`.
This rule comes before rules 30 and 41.
If the customer still names a date or an amount themselves, record the promise under sections 7 and 8.
If they decline, close as `no_promise` / `hardship`.

events.effect: do not argue, take no promise, close; a claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is a dispute

Close as `no_promise` / `dispute`.
A claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is a dispute.
Rule 39 covers only a payment of this past-due amount.
